sentences.en: They seek him here.
sentences.zh: 他们在寻找他。

sentences.en: They seek him there.
sentences.zh: 他们在寻找他。

sentences.en: His clothes are loud, but never square.
sentences.zh: 他的衣着高调，但从不循规蹈矩。

sentences.en: It will make or break him.
sentences.zh: 这会成就他，也会毁了他。

sentences.en: So he's got to buy the best because he's a dedicated follower of fashion.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须买最好的，因为他是个狂热的时尚追随者。

sentences.en: And when he does his little rounds around the boutiques of London town, eagerly pursuing all the latest fads and trends because he's a dedicated follower of fashion.
sentences.zh: 当他在伦敦城的精品店里巡视时，急切地追逐着所有最新的时尚和潮流，因为他是个狂热的时尚追随者。

sentences.en: And that, Dominic, was the Kinks, dedicated follower of fashion, which I think came out in 1966.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那是奇克斯乐队的《狂热的时尚追随者》，我想那是1966年发行的。

sentences.en: And it is a kind of mocking commentary on the status of London, the very unexpected status of London in the mid 60s as the world capital of fashion, which is today's subject,
sentences.zh: 它有点像对伦敦地位的一种嘲讽性评论，伦敦在20世纪60年代中期作为世界时尚之都的那种非常意想不到的地位，这也是我们今天的主题，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you and I were talking about this just before we started recording, weren't we, Tom?
sentences.zh: 所以你和我刚才在录音前就在谈论这个，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: We're having a dispute, a historical dispute about fashion history.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个争论，关于时尚史的历史争论。

sentences.en: Because I said, I think this is the one moment when Britain can genuinely claim to be the world capital of fashion, when British fashion is genuinely setting the trend worldwide.
sentences.zh: 因为我说，我认为这是英国真正有资格自称是世界时尚之都的时刻，当时英国时尚确实在引领全球潮流。

sentences.en: And you said, no, there was an earlier one.
sentences.zh: 而你说，不，还有一个更早的时期。

sentences.en: Yes, because I think you had forgotten the brilliant episode we did with Hilary Davidson on fashion in the age of Jane Austen,
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我想你忘了我们和希拉里·戴维森制作的关于简·奥斯汀时代时尚的精彩节目，

sentences.en: where she talked about how during the Napoleonic Wars, Britain is cut off from Paris, which is traditionally the capital of fashion.
sentences.zh: 她在节目中谈到，在拿破仑战争期间，英国与传统时尚之都巴黎被切断了联系。

sentences.en: And because of industrialization and because of the growth of shopping in London and other cities, Bath and so on, for the first time,
sentences.zh: 由于工业化，由于伦敦和其他城市（如巴斯等）购物业的发展，这是第一次，

sentences.en: you get the idea of fashion as something that is kind of changing season upon season.
sentences.zh: 你开始有了时尚的概念，认为它是一种季节更迭的事物。

sentences.en: And so very, very fleetingly in that period, the Regency period, kind of late, very late 18th century and into the first years of the 19th century,
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时期——摄政时期，18世纪末期以及19世纪初的几年里，非常非常短暂地，

sentences.en: London then is perhaps the capital of fashion.
sentences.zh: 伦敦当时或许成了时尚之都。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't last, but I take your point that the thing that's fascinating about London in the 60s is that it is not just for elites as it was back in the Regency period,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并没有持续多久，但我接受你的观点，60年代伦敦最迷人的地方在于，它不仅仅像摄政时期那样只属于精英阶层，

sentences.en: but basically for everyone.
sentences.zh: 而是基本上属于每一个人。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the selling point, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是卖点，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's how it's seen.
sentences.zh: 人们就是这样看的。

sentences.en: The whole of London is full of people in miniskirts.
sentences.zh: 整个伦敦到处都是穿着迷你裙的人。

sentences.en: Which is obviously not really true, as we will discover, but there is a sort of an overtly democratic ethos to 60s fashion, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 正如我们接下来会发现的那样，这显然并非完全真实，但60年代的时尚有一种公开的民主精神，对吧？

sentences.en: There's a democratic ethos, there is a sense of mass consumerism.
sentences.zh: 有一种民主精神，有一种大众消费主义的感觉。

sentences.en: The funny thing about a podcast about 60s fashion, there may be lots of people listening who think, well, I'm not very interested in fashion.
sentences.zh: 关于一档探讨60年代时尚的播客，有趣的是，可能会有很多听众心想，嗯，我对时尚不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: But fashion in the 60s becomes, I think, a kind of metaphor, a symbol of wider social changes.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，60年代的时尚变成了一种隐喻，一个更广泛社会变革的象征。

sentences.en: So the rise of the teenager, the rise of youth culture, but also the enormous economic recovery from the austerity of the 1940s and the privations of World War II.
sentences.zh: 因此，青少年的崛起、青年文化的兴起，还有从20世纪40年代的紧缩政策和二战的匮乏中巨大的经济复苏。

sentences.en: And the development of this sort of new, what they call in France,
sentences.zh: 以及法国人所说的这种新型的发展，

sentences.en: the 30 glorious years of full employment and economic growth and consumerism and urbanization and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 充分就业、经济增长、消费主义、城市化以及所有这些之类的事情的“光辉三十年”。

sentences.en: And fashion actually stands in, I think, for a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，时尚实际上代表了其中很大一部分内容。

sentences.en: Well, that was what is so interesting about the 60s that I now appreciate over and over again,
sentences.zh: 好吧，60年代最有趣的地方在于，我现在一次又一次地体会到，

sentences.en: is that it only really makes sense in the context of the privations of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 它只有在第二次世界大战物资匮乏的背景下才真正说得通。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That the kind of the blaze of color that you associate with the 60s exists in the kind of the monochrome context of the austerity that was the accompaniment of the war years.
sentences.zh: 你所联想到的60年代的那种色彩斑斓，存在于伴随战争年代而来的紧缩政策的那种单调背景之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这绝对正确。

sentences.en: And as we'll see with this story, it only makes sense when you go back 20 years and to see what people are, as you say, reacting againSt.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将在这个故事中所看到的，只有当你回到20年前，看看人们在——正如你所说——反抗什么时，它才说得通。

sentences.en: So what people's parents had grown up wearing, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，也就是人们的父母在成长过程中穿着的服装。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So people will have a kind of Austin Powers type, groovy baby kind of, you know, guys wearing incredibly frilly shirts.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会有奥斯汀·鲍尔斯那种“时髦宝贝”的印象，你知道的，男人们穿着极其花边的衬衫。

sentences.en: Cravats, a lot of cravats.
sentences.zh: 领巾，大量的领巾。

sentences.en: What is it in the kinks, the verse I didn't read about skin tight, frilly panties being drawn up tight.
sentences.zh: 奇克斯乐队的歌里是怎么唱的来着，我没读的那段关于被拉紧的紧身花边短裤的歌词。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: All that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And girls in kind of plastic macks and mini skirts and high boots and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 还有穿着塑料雨衣、迷你裙、高筒靴以及诸如此类行头的女孩们。

sentences.en: So put that against the kind of the image that we have of the war years.
sentences.zh: 所以，把这些与我们对战争年代的印象进行对比。

sentences.en: I guess it's a little bit unfair because we tend to think of the war years in black and white, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我想这有点不公平，因为我们倾向于用黑白来看待战争年代，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the footage is black and white.
sentences.zh: 因为当时的影像资料是黑白的。

sentences.en: But there is a kind of slightly monochrome quality to the fashion.
sentences.zh: 但这种时尚确实带有一种轻微的单色调特质。

sentences.en: Oh, there is.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: If you look at some photos of people in the 1930s and 1940s, just because of the availability of dye, actually, Tom, because the industrial processes for making clothes, I mean,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看一些20世纪30年代和40年代人们的照片，其实这只是因为染料的可用性，汤姆，因为制作衣服的工业流程，我的意思是，

sentences.en: it's expensive.
sentences.zh: 它很昂贵。

sentences.en: It's expensive to wear colored clothes.
sentences.zh: 穿彩色衣服是很昂贵的。

sentences.en: But also, of course, most people are a huge proportion of people.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有绝大多数人，很大一部分人。

sentences.en: Let's just think about Britain specifically.
sentences.zh: 让我们专门想想英国。

sentences.en: But this is actually true of the United States, France, wherever.
sentences.zh: 但其实美国、法国以及其他地方也是如此。

sentences.en: Lots of people work in factories, in coal mines, in very dirty jobs, in a very smoky environment, houses heated by coal fires or whatever.
sentences.zh: 很多人在工厂、在煤矿工作，从事非常脏的工作，在烟雾缭绕的环境中，房子靠燃煤取暖等等。

sentences.en: So it actually doesn't make sense to wear very brightly colored, delicate clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以穿颜色鲜艳、娇贵的衣服实际上并不合情合理。

sentences.en: You want to actually wear very hard wearing and dark clothes that will take the dirt effectively.
sentences.zh: 你实际上想要穿非常耐磨且颜色较深的衣服，这样才能有效地防脏。

sentences.en: Also, a massively underappreciated point, you are colder.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个极大地被低估的因素，那就是你更冷。

sentences.en: You're living in a world without central heating.
sentences.zh: 你生活在一个没有中央供暖的世界里。

sentences.en: So you wear more layers.
sentences.zh: 所以你穿更多的层数。

sentences.en: You wear your coat much more often.
sentences.zh: 你更频繁地穿大衣。

sentences.en: You might obviously wear a hat if you're a man.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个男人，你显然可能会戴帽子。

sentences.en: And you have fewer items of clothing.
sentences.zh: 而且你的衣物数量更少。

sentences.en: So let's say the outbreak of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 比方说，第二次世界大战爆发时。

sentences.en: A middle class woman in Britain would probably have about seven or eight dresses, a couple of suits, three coats, six pairs of shoes or something.
sentences.zh: 英国的一个中产阶级女性可能大约有七八条裙子、两套西装、三件大衣、六双鞋子左右。

sentences.en: A working class woman, of which there are many, of course, they might have a far smaller wardrobe, three dresses, a couple of pairs of shoes.
sentences.zh: 而工人阶级女性——当然人数众多——她们的衣橱可能会小得多，三条裙子，两双鞋。

sentences.en: A man would generally have suits, an overcoat.
sentences.zh: 一个男人通常会有几套西装和一件大衣。

sentences.en: Now, an overcoat, something like that would probably cost the equivalent in sort of the dent in your budget of about a thousand pounds in today's money.
sentences.zh: 现在，一件大衣，类似这样的东西，在你的预算中所占的比重可能相当于今天大约一千英镑的价值。

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那是很大的一笔钱。

sentences.en: That's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那是很大的一笔钱。

sentences.en: So your coat that you would buy, I mean, that might last you for 20, 30 years.
sentences.zh: 所以你买的大衣，我的意思是，可能会穿上20年、30年。

sentences.en: You might actually pass it on to your son or to a family member.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能会把它传给你的儿子或家庭成员。

sentences.en: Oh, and imagine if you leave it in the pub.
sentences.zh: 哦，想象一下如果你把它落在酒吧里。

sentences.en: Well, that's a bit, I mean, that's the kind of thing that comes up in films, in novels.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点——我的意思是，这正是电影和小说中经常出现的情节。

sentences.en: People will leave their coats behind or their hats or something.
sentences.zh: 人们会把他们的大衣或帽子什么的落在后面。

sentences.en: Run back and run into the lady.
sentences.zh: 跑回去撞上那位女士。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: It's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这可是件大事。

sentences.en: And they're heavy, they're heavy fabrics, they're dark.
sentences.zh: 而且它们很重，是厚重的面料，颜色很深。

sentences.en: So yes, there is a sort of, what you described as the monochrome world.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，确实存在一种你所描述的单色世界。

sentences.en: Of course, it is distorted in that popular imagination because of cinematography, but it's not entirely inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 当然，由于电影摄影术的原因，这种大众想象被扭曲了，但它并非完全不准确。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the war comes.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，战争爆发了。

sentences.en: So in Britain, clothing is rationed between 1941 and 1949.
sentences.zh: 所以在英国，衣物配给制从1941年一直持续到1949年。

sentences.en: So you get 66 clothing coupons a year at first, and then that is actually steadily cut as the war goes on.
sentences.zh: 所以你一开始一年有66张服装券，然后随着战争的进行，这个数字实际上在稳步削减。

sentences.en: How long does that last, the clothing ration?
sentences.zh: 服装配给制持续了多久？

sentences.en: Because isn't that the Queen's wedding dress?
sentences.zh: 因为那不正是女王的婚纱吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of problems with how many coupons she has.
sentences.zh: 关于她有多少服装券，存在着各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 情况正是如此。

sentences.en: So it actually lasts until 1949, so four years after the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上一直持续到1949年，即二战结束四年后。

sentences.en: So, and the, I mean, the sort of moment that, if we have any listeners who are old enough to remember the war, that they would remember is in 1942,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果我们的听众中有谁年纪大到还记得那场战争，他们会记得的一个时刻是1942年，

sentences.en: the Board of Trade brings in a new thing where you have to have what's called utility clothes.
sentences.zh: 贸易委员会推出了一项新规定，你必须拥有所谓的实用服装（utility clothes）。

sentences.en: And they limit the number of fabrics that are available to you, but they also limit the number of designs.
sentences.zh: 它们限制了提供给你的面料数量，同时也限制了款式的数量。

sentences.en: And there are all kinds of restrictions.
sentences.zh: 并且有各种各样的限制。

sentences.en: So to give you some examples that may sound absolutely bizarre to people now, men's shirts are not allowed to have double cuffs.
sentences.zh: 举几个对现在的人们来说可能听起来极其荒谬的例子，男式衬衫不允许有双层袖口。

sentences.en: So in other words, cuff links, you can't have kind of puffy sleeves on a shirt and on a women's shirt.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，袖扣，男式衬衫和女式衬衫上都不能有那种膨胀的衣袖。

sentences.en: Men are not allowed to have, from that point on, most people are not making double-breasted suits because it's a waste of cloth.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，大多数人不再制作双排扣西装，因为那是对布料的浪费。

sentences.en: Turn-ups on your trousers.
sentences.zh: 裤脚的翻边。

sentences.en: So trousers don't have turn-ups anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以裤子不再有翻边了。

sentences.en: I think that's probably a good thing.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是一件好事。

sentences.en: Well, it depends on the look you want.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于你想要什么造型。

sentences.en: I'm not a turn-up-on-a-trouser man, Tom, are you?
sentences.zh: 我不是那种喜欢裤子有翻边的人，汤姆，你呢？

sentences.en: No, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，我不是。

sentences.en: I think that's a kind of positive from the wall.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是战争带来的某种积极影响。

sentences.en: You're limited to three buttons per garment.
sentences.zh: 每件衣服限用三个纽扣。

sentences.en: So, you know, I mean, if you want a shirt or something with loads of buttons, you're not going to get it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我的意思是，如果你想要一件带有大量纽扣的衬衫什么的，你是买不到的。

sentences.en: And most famously, you're only allowed to use elastic on women's knickers, on nothing else.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是，你只能在女式内裤上使用松紧带，其他任何地方都不行。

sentences.en: There's even the length of a man's sock is limited to nine inches.
sentences.zh: 甚至连男袜的长度也被限制在九英寸。

sentences.en: And people actually complain.
sentences.zh: 人们竟然还抱怨。

sentences.en: Some people complain.
sentences.zh: 有些人抱怨。

sentences.en: They say, well, I wanted longer socks.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，我想要更长的袜子。

sentences.en: What about schoolboys?
sentences.zh: 那男生呢？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I would say schoolboys probably, they got away with it because their legs are shorter.
sentences.zh: 我想男生可能占了便宜，因为他们的腿比较短。

sentences.en: If you're a very small schoolboy, yes.
sentences.zh: 如果你个子非常矮，是的。

sentences.en: I was a very short schoolboy, so I would have been laughing.
sentences.zh: 我曾是个个子很矮的男生，所以我当时肯定会偷着乐。

sentences.en: But that continues after the war.
sentences.zh: 但这在战后仍在继续。

sentences.en: So in the late 1940s, because there's not much leather, the shoe industry is kind of restricted.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪40年代末，由于皮革短缺，制鞋业受到了一定限制。

sentences.en: The government had adopted a slogan in 1943, make, do and mend, which you and I will, I mean, we grew up with people talking about make, do and mend, didn't me?
sentences.zh: 政府在1943年通过了一条标语：自行制作、凑合使用并修补（make, do and mend），你和我——我的意思是，我们是在人们谈论“自行制作、凑合使用并修补”的环境中长大的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's actually entered the, certainly in Britain, it's entered the English language as a, we don't think of it as having a kind of wartime sort of ethos.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它实际上已经进入了——当然在英国，它已经进入了英语语言，我们并不认为它带有某种战时精神。

sentences.en: And that's not lifted until 1949.
sentences.zh: 直到1949年，这个限制才被取消。

sentences.en: So the kind of clothes that people were wearing, just last note on the war, they're very boxy, kind of utilitarian.
sentences.zh: 所以人们穿的衣服——关于战争的最后一点，它们非常方正，带有一种功利主义色彩。

sentences.en: There's obviously a kind of militaristic vogue.
sentences.zh: 显然有一种军事化风潮。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a status, I suppose, in a funny way, in wearing very sort of boxy utilitarian clothes.
sentences.zh: 以一种搞笑的方式来看，穿着非常方正、功利主义的服装似乎带有一种身份地位。

sentences.en: And these are the DMOB suits that discharged soldiers get at the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 这些就是复员军人在战争结束时领到的退伍军人西装（DMOB suits）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're cheap suits.
sentences.zh: 而且它们是廉价西装。

sentences.en: You're a young man, that's the only suit you own.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个年轻男子，那是你拥有的唯一一套西装。

sentences.en: And people complain about the DMOB suits.
sentences.zh: 人们抱怨这些退伍军人西装。

sentences.en: Obviously, they say that the arm comes off and it's rubbish and it doesn't look good and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们说袖子会掉下来，简直是垃圾，看起来不好看，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But at the same time, something quite democratic about it because everyone's wearing the same suit.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它又有着相当民主的一面，因为每个人穿的都是同一套西装。

sentences.en: Is there a sense still of le style anglais, the look of the English gentleman?
sentences.zh: 是否仍然有一种英伦风范（le style anglais）的感觉，即英国绅士的造型？

sentences.en: Is that still a thing?
sentences.zh: 那还是个流行趋势吗？

sentences.en: Fine tailoring on Savile Row?
sentences.zh: 萨维尔街的高级定制服装？

sentences.en: Well, that's at the very top end.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是最高端的东西。

sentences.en: I think generally English clothes are very conservative, actually, in the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 我认为总体而言，20世纪40年代的英国服装其实非常保守。

sentences.en: The image of English fashion abroad certainly is very conservative.
sentences.zh: 英国时尚在海外的形象当然非常保守。

sentences.en: I don't think people in France, Italy, the traditional powerhouses of fashion, they're not looking to London and saying, gosh, is London going to lead the way after the war?
sentences.zh: 我认为法国和意大利这些传统的时尚大国的人们，当时并没有寄希望于伦敦，说“天哪，战后伦敦会引领潮流吗？”

sentences.en: I mean, nobody would ever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根本没有人会这么想。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And so Paris has been under German occupation.
sentences.zh: 所以巴黎一直处于德国占领之下。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But in the wake of the war, famously, it kind of, you know, it's the phoenix from the ashes.
sentences.zh: 但在战后，众所周知，它有点像浴火重生的凤凰。

sentences.en: It's the butterfly re-emerging and taking wing, isn't it, with the new look?
sentences.zh: 这就是蝴蝶重新破茧而出、展翅飞翔的新面貌，对吧？

sentences.en: It is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全没错。

sentences.en: So this is a guy called Christian Dior, who is the, he's the, very glamorously, Tom, he's the son of a fertilizer manufacturer from Normandy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个叫克里斯汀·迪奥的家伙，他呀，他是，很有魅力地，汤姆，他是诺曼底一个化肥制造商的儿子。

sentences.en: And he makes uniforms for German officers in the war, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在战争期间为德国军官制作军服，对吧？

sentences.en: Notoriously.
sentences.zh: 恶名昭彰。

sentences.en: Well, German officers' wives.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是德国军官的妻子们。

sentences.en: Ah, okay.
sentences.zh: 啊，好吧。

sentences.en: I'm being unfair on him then.
sentences.zh: 那我对他有点不公平了。

sentences.en: So actually what happens is Dior wanted to be an artist and he ended up sketching for fashion house and then he ends up designing the clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上发生的情况是，迪奥想成为一名艺术家，他最后为时装屋画草图，然后开始设计服装。

sentences.en: And yes, in the war, during the occupation, he does design clothes or he's said to have designed clothes for the wives of German officers.
sentences.zh: 是的，在战争期间，在占领时期，他确实设计过衣服，或者说据称他为德国军官的妻子们设计过衣服。

sentences.en: I mean, to be fair, I don't think this is some sign of some latent Nazism in Christian Dior.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，公平地说，我不认为这代表克里斯汀·迪奥身上有什么潜在的纳粹主义倾向。

sentences.en: I mean, he's living under the occupation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他生活在占领区。

sentences.en: He has no choice, effectively.
sentences.zh: 实际上他别无选择。

sentences.en: I mean, lots of people are, I don't know, baking croissants for German officers or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我是说，很多人都在，我不知道，为德国军官烤牛角面包之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, fair enough.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也是。

sentences.en: But then there is this absolute landmark moment, which all fashion historians and anybody interested in the history of clothes will know, which is the 12th of February, 1947,
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了一个绝对具有里程碑意义的时刻，所有时装历史学家以及任何对服装历史感兴趣的人都会知道，那就是1947年2月12日，

sentences.en: when he unveils his first sort of individual collection.
sentences.zh: 当时他推出了他个人的首个系列产品。

sentences.en: And this is the birth of what's called the new look.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“新风貌”的诞生。

sentences.en: So everything that we described, the sort of very austere, utilitarian look of clothes, Dior ditches all that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们所描述的一切，那种非常简朴、实用主义的服装风格，迪奥把这些全抛弃了。

sentences.en: And his clothes and their women's clothes, they are very glamorous, narrow waists and then great sweeping kind of skirts and dresses,
sentences.zh: 他的服装以及女装，都极具魅力，细腰，然后是巨大大摆的半身裙和连衣裙，

sentences.en: emphasizing sort of voluptuousness and sexuality and curves and lush.
sentences.zh: 强调了一种丰腴、性感、曲线美和华丽感。

sentences.en: They're really kind of lush, glamorous clothes.
sentences.zh: 它们真的是那种华丽、迷人的服装。

sentences.en: And of course, against the backdrop of a Europe that is, I mean, every country in Europe is full of bombed out buildings, homeless people, poverty stricken.
sentences.zh: 当然，在一片废墟的欧洲背景下——我是说，欧洲每个国家都充满了被炸毁的建筑、无家可归的人、极度的贫困。

sentences.en: There's a sense of escapism to the new look.
sentences.zh: “新风貌”带有一种逃避现实的感觉。

sentences.en: And presumably it has to be Paris where this happens.
sentences.zh: 而且这种事大概只能在巴黎发生。

sentences.en: No other city would have this impact because Paris has this legacy as the great center of fashion.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个城市能产生这种影响，因为巴黎作为伟大的时尚中心拥有这样的历史遗产。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this is evidence that Paris is back after the humiliations and sufferings of the war.
sentences.zh: 这证明了在经历了战争的屈辱和苦难之后，巴黎又回来了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's interesting that the phrase, the new look, is coined by an American journalist who is watching the unveiling of Dior's show.
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，“新风貌”这个词是由一位美国记者在观看迪奥时装秀发布会时创造的。

sentences.en: And she says, oh, Christiane, what a new look you've adopted.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，克里斯汀，你采用了多么崭新的风貌啊。

sentences.en: But the very fact that there are journalists there to watch it tells you that it's the focus of attention.
sentences.zh: 但现场有记者去观看这一事实本身就说明，它是人们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: It's the focus of the world's attention.
sentences.zh: 它是世界瞩目的焦点。

sentences.en: And, you know, the clothes are reproduced in English magazines and English newspapers, indeed, in American magazines and newspapers.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这些服装被刊登在英国杂志和英国报纸上，当然，也登在美国的杂志和报纸上。

sentences.en: That wouldn't be the case if they were being unveiled.
sentences.zh: 如果它们只是在别处发布，就不会是这个样子了。

sentences.en: And, you know, it pains me to say it, Tom, but if they're being unveiled in Birmingham, that would not be the, the world would not be watching.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，说这话让我很难过，汤姆，但如果它们是在伯明翰发布的话，那绝不会，全世界都不会关注。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 也是。

sentences.en: So it's sort of an illusion, actually, the new look, because most people can't afford new look clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，“新风貌”某种程度上是一种幻觉，因为大多数人根本买不起新风貌的服装。

sentences.en: They are still living in this sort of world.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然生活在那种世界里。

sentences.en: I mean, rationing is still going for another two years in Britain, but it's an aspiration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英国的配给制还要持续两年，但这是一种向往。

sentences.en: And does this percolate through into kind of mass market clothing in, in Britain?
sentences.zh: 这会渗透到英国的大众市场服装中吗？

sentences.en: Slowly.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地。

sentences.en: In the long run?
sentences.zh: 从长远来看？

sentences.en: Yes, in the long run.
sentences.zh: 是的，从长远来看。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代。

sentences.en: So actually what happens is after 1949, when the Russians are lifted, the British economy takes another two or three years to really sort of fire up again.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上发生的情况是，在1949年配给制取消后，英国经济又花了两年或三年的时间才真正重新恢复活力。

sentences.en: And when it does fire up again, obviously people are buying, you know, different clothes.
sentences.zh: 当它真正恢复活力时，人们显然在购买，你知道，不同的衣服。

sentences.en: They're buying more, more lightweight clothes, more colorful.
sentences.zh: 他们购买更多、更轻便的衣服，更加五颜六色。

sentences.en: They're keen to sort of put the wartime experience and the kind of the heaviness behind them.
sentences.zh: 他们渴望把战时的经历和那种沉重感抛在脑后。

sentences.en: That said, when you look at pictures of the sort of early to mid 1950s and young people, I mean, if you look at some of the famous young people in Britain of the early to mid 50s.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，当你看到50年代初到中期以及年轻人的照片时——我的意思是，如果你看看50年代初中期英国的一些名人。

sentences.en: So, I mean, Kingsley Amos, Philip Larkin, the writers who come of age in that period or people like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，金斯利·艾米斯、菲利普·拉金，那些在那个时期成名的作家或者类似的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They're wearing tweed suits, heavy shoes, a tie, often an overcoat.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着花呢西装，沉重的鞋子，打着领带，通常还穿着一件外衣。

sentences.en: They are wearing versions of the sort of heavy clothes that their parents would have worn.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着他们父母可能会穿的那种厚重服装的变体。

sentences.en: So kind of intellectual young men who like jazz are still wearing suits, right?
sentences.zh: 所以喜欢爵士乐的知识分子青年仍然穿着西装，对吧？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实穿着。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实穿着。

sentences.en: But we've talked about the influence of Paris.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经讨论过巴黎的影响了。

sentences.en: What about the influence of America?
sentences.zh: 那美国的影响呢？

sentences.en: Because American troops have been over in Britain and there's a kind of a sense that America is vibrant, colorful, wealthy, relaxed.
sentences.zh: 因为美军曾在英国驻扎过，而且人们有一种感觉，美国是充满活力、色彩斑斓、富有而又轻松的。

sentences.en: Everything that bombed out stuffy Britain isn't.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是被炸毁且古板的英国所不具备的。

sentences.en: Is that having an impact on fashion?
sentences.zh: 这对时尚有影响吗？

sentences.en: Hollywood always has an impact on fashion.
sentences.zh: 好莱坞对时尚总是有影响的。

sentences.en: So even in the 1930s, I say even in the 1930s, especially in the 1930s, people are often complaining,
sentences.zh: 所以即使在20世纪30年代——我说即使在30年代，特别是30年代，人们经常抱怨，

sentences.en: sort of Daily Express columnists are complaining that young women in Britain are copying American fashions.
sentences.zh: 《每日快报》的专栏作家们抱怨英国的年轻女性在模仿美国的时尚。

sentences.en: But actually, the fashions they're copying are not so different from what they're wearing themselves.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，她们模仿的时尚与她们自己穿的并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: They might be a particular cut of a skirt or something like that, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 可能只是裙子的某种剪裁或类似的东西，但并非如此。

sentences.en: People aren't all dressing in jeans or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 人们并没有全都穿上牛仔裤或诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: What you do have is people who are copying, for example, biker films in the mid 1950s.
sentences.zh: 你确实会看到有人在模仿，比如20世纪50年代中期的飞车党电影。

sentences.en: So that's the leather jackets.
sentences.zh: 也就是皮夹克。

sentences.en: So that's the sort of ancestors of the rockers.
sentences.zh: 所以那是摇滚客的某种祖先。

sentences.en: We'll come to the modern rockers in a second.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿就会谈到现代的摇滚客。

sentences.en: And you do have a group of people now who are different, who have not really existed except in embryonic form in the 30s before.
sentences.zh: 现在确实有一群与众不同的人，他们在30年代之前除了以雏形存在外，并没有真正存在过。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is teenagers.
sentences.zh: 当然，那就是青少年。

sentences.en: So teenagers have money.
sentences.zh: 所以青少年有钱了。

sentences.en: So much of this story is about young women.
sentences.zh: 这个故事很大一部分是关于年轻女性的。

sentences.en: But actually, the first example of a sort of fashion subculture in the 50s is the teddy boys.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，50年代某种时尚亚文化的第一个例子是泰迪男孩。

sentences.en: And teddy boy, the teddy, is Edward VII, right?
sentences.zh: 而泰迪男孩的“泰迪”，指的是爱德华七世，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the Edwardian period.
sentences.zh: 那是爱德华时代。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the weird thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很奇怪。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The new look also is kind of very influenced by the sweep and the color and the cut of Edwardian dress.
sentences.zh: “新风貌”也深受爱德华时代服饰的摆幅、颜色和剪裁的影响。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because actually, if you think about what was very cool in, let's say, the 20s, it was a very androgynous look for women, for example.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，如果你想想比方说在20年代什么最酷，那对女性来说是一种非常雌雄同体的造型。

sentences.en: Let's say flappers, most famously.
sentences.zh: 比方说飞来波女郎，最典型不过了。

sentences.en: So the new look is actually looking back to the much more kind of romantic, glamorous fashions of the Edwardian period.
sentences.zh: 所以“新风貌”实际上是在回溯爱德华时代那种更具浪漫色彩、更迷人的时尚。

sentences.en: And do you think that's because there's a sense that it's not just the Second World War, but the First World War,
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是因为人们觉得不仅是第二次世界大战，还有第一次世界大战，

sentences.en: that there's been this continuous process of conflict and convulsion?
sentences.zh: 经历了一连串持续的冲突和动荡？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: And therefore, perhaps the Edwardian period is seen as, you know, something to get back to.
sentences.zh: 因此，也许爱德华时代被视为，你知道的，某种可以回归的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's where you would look to.
sentences.zh: 对，我是说，那是你会去寻找的方向。

sentences.en: It's where you would look to.
sentences.zh: 那是你会去寻找的方向。

sentences.en: Because people aren't going to look back to the 1920s flapper fashions because they're...
sentences.zh: 因为人们不会回溯到20世纪20年代的飞来波女郎时尚，因为它们……

sentences.en: Yeah, you know what's coming.
sentences.zh: 对，你知道接下来会怎样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's the day before yesterday.
sentences.zh: 那是前天的事了。

sentences.en: But yeah, so with the Teddy Boys, Edwardian, as you said, that again, it's not, I mean, it's so different from the new look,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，所以对于泰迪男孩来说，就像你说的爱德华时代风格，这又一次，它不是——我的意思是，它与“新风貌”截然不同，

sentences.en: but actually it's not dissimilar in the sense that it's an attempt to inject a kind of romanticism and a glamour to clothing.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，从它试图为服装注入一种浪漫主义和魅力的角度来看，它又并非不相似。

sentences.en: But that is bottom up, right?
sentences.zh: 但那是自下而上的，对吧？

sentences.en: No, not initially.
sentences.zh: 不，最初不是。

sentences.en: This is interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: So people do think the Teddy Boys are bottom up, but actually what seems to have happened, and of course, when you're writing about fashion history,
sentences.zh: 所以人们确实认为泰迪男孩是自下而上的，但实际上发生的情况似乎是——当然，当你撰写时尚史时，

sentences.en: you're actually just picking up fragments of stuff and trying to get some sense of a narrative out of it.
sentences.zh: 你实际上只是在收集零碎的东西，并试图从中理出某种叙事线索。

sentences.en: You know, what are people wearing here?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里的人们穿什么？

sentences.en: What are people wearing there?
sentences.zh: 那里的人们穿什么？

sentences.en: There's some suggestion that actually rich, you know, upper middle class young men at the end of the 1940s, as rationing is coming to an end,
sentences.zh: 有迹象表明，实际上在40年代末，随着配给制的结束，随着有一点点钱可花，富有的，你知道的，上中产阶级的年轻人，在努力让自己看起来更别致一点。

sentences.en: as there's a little bit more money around, are making a little bit of effort to just look a bit fancier.
sentences.zh: 所以一个别致的领子，或者一件漂亮的马甲，或者稍微窄一点的裤子之类的东西。

sentences.en: So a fancy collar or a nice waistcoat or sort of narrower trousers and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以一个别致的领子，或者一件漂亮的马甲，或者稍微窄一点的裤子之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then basically what seems to have happened is that percolated down.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上发生的事情似乎是，这股风潮向下渗透了。

sentences.en: Let's say you're 21 and you fancy yourself as quite cool.
sentences.zh: 假设你21岁，你自认为挺酷的。

sentences.en: Not that you would have used that expression.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你会用这个词。

sentences.en: You wear a more colourful shirt.
sentences.zh: 你穿着色彩更鲜艳的衬衫。

sentences.en: You sweep your hair up in a quiff.
sentences.zh: 你把头发向上梳成蓬松的发髻。

sentences.en: You wear kind of tapered trousers.
sentences.zh: 你穿着某种锥形裤。

sentences.en: You have kind of black boots.
sentences.zh: 你穿着某种黑色靴子。

sentences.en: And these are the Teddy Boys.
sentences.zh: 这些就是泰迪男孩。

sentences.en: So what the press describe as gay dog clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以媒体将其描述为花花公子的服装。

sentences.en: Gay dog clothes.
sentences.zh: 花花公子的服装。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there's a description in a book called Hurry On Down, which was written in 1953 by a friend of Kingsley Amos called John Wayne.
sentences.zh: 所以在一本名为《快快向下》的书中有这样一段描述，该书于1953年由金斯利·艾米斯的一位名叫约翰·韦恩的朋友所写。

sentences.en: And he's talking about knots of youths.
sentences.zh: 他在谈论成群结队的年轻人。

sentences.en: And he says most of them.
sentences.zh: 他说他们大多数人。

sentences.en: John Wayne as in the cowboy.
sentences.zh: 约翰·韦恩，就像那个牛仔一样。

sentences.en: Not the cowboy.
sentences.zh: 不是那个牛仔。

sentences.en: And he says most of them wore blue or brown suits and shoes with pointed toes.

sentences.zh: 嗯，传统上来说，如果你在上学，如果你只有六岁，你不会穿着那种全长及地的裙子，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, you would wear a shorter skirt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你会穿短一点的裙子。

sentences.en: And so shorter skirts for adult women make them look.
sentences.zh: 所以成年女性穿短裙会让她们看起来……

sentences.en: Fantalize them a bit.
sentences.zh: 有点把她们幻想化了。

sentences.en: Fantalizes them a little bit.
sentences.zh: 让她们带有一点幻想色彩。

sentences.en: So knickerbockers she has, she has kind of knee socks.
sentences.zh: 所以她有灯笼裤，她有那种及膝袜。

sentences.en: The patterns that Mary Quant uses, so polka dots, stripes.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·Quant使用的图案，比如波点、条纹。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: I'd never thought of that.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过这一点。

sentences.en: Again, they are equated with children's clothes.
sentences.zh: 同样，它们与童装划上了等号。

sentences.en: Even the fabrics, Tom.
sentences.zh: 甚至面料也是如此，汤姆。

sentences.en: Gingham, most obviously, or tartan.
sentences.zh: 格子呢，最明显的是维希格，或者是苏格兰呢。

sentences.en: Those are things that, you know, they are seen as the fashions.
sentences.zh: 那些是你所知道的，它们被视为时尚的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, you mentioned the Enid Blyton famous.
sentences.zh: 哦，你提到了伊妮德·布莱顿的著名作品。

sentences.en: They're kind of school uniform.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像校服。

sentences.en: They're school uniform.
sentences.zh: 它们就是校服。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're the things that Enid Blyton's kids would wear in the stories.
sentences.zh: 它们是伊妮德·布莱顿的孩子们在故事里会穿的衣服。

sentences.en: They're jolly, bright, informal.
sentences.zh: 它们令人愉快、明亮、随意。

sentences.en: But again, also, it's backward looking, right?
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也是一种向后看，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, as with the Teddy Boys, as with Sergeant Pepper in due course, there's a sense of people
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像泰迪男孩一样，就像后来的《佩珀中士》一样，有一种人们直接从一个被上一代人视为毫无时尚感定义的过去的时代汲取灵感的意味。

sentences.en: drawing inspiration directly from a past that a previous generation had come to seem as the definition of unfashionable.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于走在时尚前沿的人来说，高度不时尚的东西突然变得时尚了。

sentences.en: And therefore, for those on the cutting edge, the highly unfashionable suddenly becomes fashionable.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们意识到这是一个一直延续到现在的持续循环。

sentences.en: And we're aware of that as an ongoing cycle right the way up into the present.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在人们一直在写关于这方面的内容。

sentences.en: Well, people write about that all the time now.
sentences.zh: 流行文化在多大程度上在吞噬自身？

sentences.en: To what extent does popular culture cannibalize itself?
sentences.zh: 我们不再生产任何新东西，而只是不断地吞噬过去。

sentences.en: We cease to produce anything new and we're constantly just cannibalizing the paSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以合乎逻辑地认为，甚至在此时，实际上，他们吞噬的是20世纪20年代。

sentences.en: You could reasonably argue that even at this point, effectively, what they're cannibalizing is the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 所以，也就是飞女郎的造型。

sentences.en: So, the flapper look.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 飞女郎的造型和60年代的造型之间有着明确的连续性。

sentences.en: There is a definite continuity between the flapper look and the sort of the 60s look.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论如何，玛丽·Quant设计了这些在当时被认为是具有突破性的服装。

sentences.en: So, Mary Quant, anyway, she does these clothes that are seen at the time as tremendously groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 现在，关于这一点有几点要说。

sentences.en: Now, just a couple of things about this.
sentences.zh: 首先，她当时吹嘘说，这是一种非常60年代式的吹嘘。

sentences.en: First of all, she boasts at the time, and it's a very 60s boaSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们总是把这与他们在20世纪60年代生产的任何东西联系在一起。

sentences.en: I mean, people always make this about anything they produce in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 她说，这是无阶级的。

sentences.en: She says, it's classless.
sentences.zh: 在我们的店里，你会发现女公爵与打字员挤在一起买同样的裙子。

sentences.en: In our shops, you will find duchesses jostling with typists to buy the same dresses.
sentences.zh: 这不是真的。

sentences.en: This is not true.
sentences.zh: 因此，我在我的一本书里——我想是在《白热》里——举了一个她在1960年风靡一时的围裙裙的例子。

sentences.en: So, I gave the example in, I think, in one of my books, In White Heat, of a pinafore dress that she made that was in vogue in 1960.
sentences.zh: 那件衣服售价17畿尼。

sentences.en: And that cost 17 guineas.
sentences.zh: 这相当于一个在办公室工作的年轻女性三周的工资。

sentences.en: And that's the equivalent of three weeks' wages for a young woman who works in an office.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，她竟然想宣称这一点。

sentences.en: But it's interesting that she would want to make that claim.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她大概不会想在十年前宣称这一点，当时价格才是全部的重点。

sentences.en: I mean, she wouldn't have wanted to make that claim presumably a decade before, where the price is the whole point.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想你会说这是一个社会民主的时代。

sentences.en: It's a social democratic age, I think you would say.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代和60年代，依然带着一丝二战结束时留下的平均主义的痕迹。

sentences.en: The 1950s and 1960s, there's still a hint of the leftover egalitarianism from the end of World War II.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充分就业的时代，一个生活水平飙升的时代，

sentences.en: It's an age of full employment, an age of the surging living standards,
sentences.zh: 一个对被视为古老建制派的老派和势利眼进行反抗的时代。

sentences.en: an age when there's a reaction against what's seen as the stuffiness and the snobbery of the old establishment.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一种感觉，即源自街头的时尚具有了前所未有的公信力吗？

sentences.en: But is there also a sense that fashion that is coming from the streets has a credibility that hadn't been there before?
sentences.zh: 有这种感觉吗？

sentences.en: Is there any sense of that?
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种轻微的感觉，有人在挑战那种古老的、高度自上而下由时装屋指导的造型。

sentences.en: I think there's a slight sense there are people challenging the old, very top-down fashion house directed look.
sentences.zh: 它们是一种新的载体。

sentences.en: They're a new vehicle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们马上就会讨论精品店。

sentences.en: I mean, we'll get into boutiques in just a second.
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论之前，关于玛丽·Quant，其实她的一点是，尽管她最初的店铺确实是一家针对斯隆广场人群的店，

sentences.en: Just before we do that, Mary Quant, one of the things about her actually is although her initial shop is really a shop for kind of Sloan Square people,
sentences.zh: 也就是切尔西那些相当时髦高贵的人，但她确实真正走向了大众市场。

sentences.en: so quite posh people in Chelsea, she does become genuinely mass market.
sentences.zh: 因此，成立了一个名为伦敦时装屋集团的新组织，它组织伦敦时装周，并组织前往巴黎和纽约的巡演。

sentences.en: So there has been formed a new group called the London Fashion House Group, which organises London Fashion Weeks and organises tours of Paris and New York.
sentences.zh: 而她一直走在最前沿。

sentences.en: And she is always at the forefront in that.
sentences.zh: 她实际上与J.C.彭尼签了一笔交易。

sentences.en: And she actually signs a deal with J.C.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的美国听众会知道J.C.彭尼这个名字。

sentences.en: Penney.
sentences.zh: 它是60年代美国最大的服装连锁店之一。

sentences.en: So our American listeners will know the name J.C.
sentences.zh: 他们在1700家美国分店销售她品牌的服装。

sentences.en: Penney.
sentences.zh: 她是那个时代第一位英国设计师，她的服装你可以在俄克拉荷马州的塔尔萨、洛杉矶、芝加哥或任何地方买到。

sentences.en: It's one of the biggest clothing chains in the United States in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一种真正的全球影响力。

sentences.en: And they sell her label clothes in 1,700 American branches.
sentences.zh: 正是那种欢快、幼稚的外观让人觉得新颖，我认为不同寻常，因为它被认为是不保守的。

sentences.en: She's the first British designer of that generation whose clothes, you can buy them in Tulsa, Oklahoma, in Los Angeles, in Chicago, wherever.
sentences.zh: 你不需要在每条译文里

sentences.en: You know, it's a genuine kind of global reach.
sentences.zh: 重复这些内容。

sentences.en: And it's that sort of jolly, infantile kind of look that is novel, I think, that is unusual because it's seen as unconservative.
sentences.zh: 因为JSON要求完整。

sentences.en: And informal and all of those things.
sentences.zh: 而且非常随性，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And when you say infantile, the look isn't just kind of short skirts.
sentences.zh: 当你说是幼稚风格时，这种外观不只是短裙那么简单。

sentences.en: It's also going back to the slightly thinner look of flappers in the 20s, right?
sentences.zh: 它也回归到了20年代飞跃女郎那种稍微纤细的外观，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是。

sentences.en: No curves or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 没有曲线或者诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: We'll sort of deconstruct that a bit later on, I think, because it's a fascinating thing.
sentences.zh: 我想我们稍后会稍微解构一下这个，因为这是一个迷人的话题。

sentences.en: And it becomes even more pronounced later in the 60s when you get to Twiggy.
sentences.zh: 到了60年代后期，随着崔姬的出现，这种风格变得更加明显。

sentences.en: The rejection of the curves of the new look and the rejection of, I mean, I think just as a spoiler, lots of people at the time talk about it as a rejection of motherhood,
sentences.zh: 对新风貌曲线的排斥，以及对——我的意思是，我觉得作为一个剧透，当时许多人将其谈作是对母性的排斥，

sentences.en: a rejection of female maturity.
sentences.zh: 对女性成熟的排斥。

sentences.en: And a huge obsession with youth, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，还有对青春的极度痴迷。

sentences.en: As early as 1959, Vogue has an editorial where they say that the word young is becoming the persuasive adjective for all fashions, hairstyles and ways of life.
sentences.zh: 早在1959年，《Vogue》杂志就发表了一篇社论，他们在文中表示，“年轻”一词正在成为所有时尚、发型和生活方式最具说服力的形容词。

sentences.en: Now, that was just not true.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: We think of that as true now, but that really wasn't true 20 or 30 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们现在觉得这是真的，但在20或30年前，这可真不是真的。

sentences.en: The obvious reason being that young people didn't have very much money.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的原因是，年轻人没有多少钱。

sentences.en: So there's absolutely no point in marketing all your stuff to them.
sentences.zh: 所以把你们所有的东西都营销给他们是毫无意义的。

sentences.en: And actually, what happens is, because there's not much money, once you become an adult, you buy adult clothes that will hopefully,
sentences.zh: 事实上，情况是这样的，因为没有多少钱，一旦你成年了，你就会买成人的衣服，希望——

sentences.en: that overcoat that's worth the equivalent of £1,000, you're hoping that that will last you till you're dead.
sentences.zh: 那件相当于1000英镑的大衣，你希望它能穿到你死的那天。

sentences.en: Yeah, you don't want to change it every...
sentences.zh: 对，你可不想每隔……

sentences.en: You don't want to have to change it every four weeks.
sentences.zh: 你可不想每四周就换一次。

sentences.en: But by 1959, people are talking about disposable fashion, about clothes that you will wear for just one year, and then you will ditch, even when you're 1920.
sentences.zh: 但到了1959年，人们开始谈论一次性时尚，谈论那些你只穿一年就会扔掉的衣服，哪怕你才19、20岁。

sentences.en: So you talked about how Mary Quant's first boutique is actually very, very expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以你之前谈到玛丽·Quant的第一家精品店其实非常非常贵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's the process whereby these clothes start to percolate down?
sentences.zh: 这些服装开始向下渗透的过程是怎样的？

sentences.en: So the classic figure is the Dolly Bird.
sentences.zh: 所以典型的代表人物就是“多莉鸟”。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 对，是的，没错。

sentences.en: These are the girls who are going to, you know, screaming at the Beatles or Scylla Black, I guess.
sentences.zh: 这些女孩，你知道的，会冲着披头士乐队或者西拉·布莱克尖叫，我猜。

sentences.en: Scylla Black.
sentences.zh: 西拉·布莱克。

sentences.en: And nobody outside Britain will know who Scylla Black was.
sentences.zh: 英国以外没有人会知道西拉·布莱克是谁。

sentences.en: But Google her.
sentences.zh: 但你可以谷歌一下她。

sentences.en: Look her up.
sentences.zh: 去查查她。

sentences.en: So the big phenomenon is the rise of the independent little boutique.
sentences.zh: 所以最大的现象是独立小精品店的崛起。

sentences.en: Previously, you bought your clothes often from a department store or a shop like Marks & Spencer.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，你买衣服通常是从百货公司或玛莎百货这样的商店购买。

sentences.en: So a high street store.
sentences.zh: 也就是商业街的商店。

sentences.en: Now those department stores, even quite small, not small towns, but medium-sized towns might have a department store.
sentences.zh: 现在那些百货公司，甚至是相当小的——也不是小镇，而是中等规模的城镇，都可能会有一家百货公司。

sentences.en: These are places with long leases and high rents.
sentences.zh: 这些地方租期长、租金高。

sentences.en: Boutiques are very different.
sentences.zh: 精品店则非常不同。

sentences.en: They have short-term leases and they're paying low rents.
sentences.zh: 它们的租期较短，支付的租金也很低。

sentences.en: The shop is often down a side street.
sentences.zh: 店铺通常在偏街小巷里。

sentences.en: It's not on the main road because it's too expensive.
sentences.zh: 它不在主干道上，因为那里太贵了。

sentences.en: And there are young people who, you know, who open them.
sentences.zh: 而且开店的都是些年轻人，你知道的。

sentences.en: They may only be around for two or three years.
sentences.zh: 它们可能只开两三年。

sentences.en: The atmosphere is much more informal.
sentences.zh: 这里的氛围要随性得多。

sentences.en: And it's actually through those shops opening in places across Britain that the Mary Quant look is kind of diffused.
sentences.zh: 事实上正是通过这些在英国各地开业的店铺，玛丽·Quant的风格才得以某种程度的普及。

sentences.en: And people are copying it because they've seen it in magazines and things, which, again, we'll get on to.
sentences.zh: 人们在效仿它，因为他们在杂志之类的媒介上看到了它，我们等会儿也会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: And the Dolly Bird.
sentences.zh: 还有“多莉鸟”。

sentences.en: So we said before that the people who are really driving this are young women or young girls stroke women between the ages of, let's say, 13, 14 and maybe 24, 25.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前说过，真正推动这一潮流的是年轻女性或年轻女孩（姑且算作女性吧），年龄大约在13、14岁到24、25岁之间。

sentences.en: And they absolutely, you know, the Mary Quant look, it's modern, it's informal, it's quite androgynous.
sentences.zh: 而且她们绝对——你知道的，玛丽·Quant的风格，它是现代的、随性的、相当中性的。

sentences.en: That definitely has begun to conquer the mass market by the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪60年代初，它绝对已经开始征服大众市场了。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么做到的？

sentences.en: I mean, how are people, say, outside London?
sentences.zh: 我是说，伦敦以外的人们，比方说，

sentences.en: Yeah, how do they see it?
sentences.zh: 对，他们是怎么看到的？

sentences.en: Outside the West End.
sentences.zh: 在西区之外。

sentences.en: How are they coming across these fashions?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何接触到这些时尚的？

sentences.en: Magazines or TV or what?
sentences.zh: 杂志、电视还是别的什么？

sentences.en: TV is part of it.
sentences.zh: 电视是其中一部分。

sentences.en: And so by the late 1950s, both the BBC and ITV, their commercial competitor, are running weekly pop music programs, sort of Ready, Steady, Go, Six, Five Special.
sentences.zh: 因此到了20世纪50年代末，BBC和ITV（它们的商业竞争对手）都在播放每周一次的流行音乐节目，比如《Ready, Steady, Go》、《Six, Five Special》。

sentences.en: These kind of programs in which you see pop groups who are wearing these clothes, but you also see the audience.
sentences.zh: 在这些节目里，你能看到穿着这些服装的流行乐队，也能看到观众。

sentences.en: Of course, not everybody has a TV at this point.
sentences.zh: 当然，此时并非每个人都拥有电视。

sentences.en: So even more important than TV, I would argue, are magazines.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，比电视更重要的其实是杂志。

sentences.en: Women's magazines had always been massive.
sentences.zh: 女性杂志一直以来都规模庞大。

sentences.en: So there's a magazine called Woman.
sentences.zh: 有一本杂志叫《Woman》。

sentences.en: And in the late 1950s, there's some extraordinary statistic that out of all the British women between the ages of 16 and 44, half of them read Woman magazine.
sentences.zh: 在50年代末，有一个惊人的统计数据：在所有年龄在16岁到44岁之间的英国女性中，有一半的人阅读《Woman》杂志。

sentences.en: Wow, that is a stupefying figure.
sentences.zh: 哇，这真是一个令人咋舌的数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But also the new thing is magazines for teenage girls, for very young women.
sentences.zh: 但新出现的事物是面向十几岁女孩、面向极年轻女性的杂志。

sentences.en: And they obviously didn't really exist before because they didn't have the money.
sentences.zh: 显然，以前这些杂志并不真的存在，因为她们没有钱。

sentences.en: Now there are magazines like Romeo, Mirabelle, Boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 现在有了像《Romeo》、《Mirabelle》、《Boyfriend》这样的杂志。

sentences.en: And the most famous one is called Honey.
sentences.zh: 其中最著名的一本叫做《Honey》。

sentences.en: Honey was launched in 1960, circulation at 140,000.
sentences.zh: 《Honey》创刊于1960年，发行量达到了14万册。

sentences.en: Their slogan, the Teddy Boys is gay dog clothes.
sentences.zh: 它们的标语——泰迪男孩是时髦的狗衣服。

sentences.en: Their slogan is young, gay and going far.
sentences.zh: 它们的标语是“年轻、时髦、前程远大”。

sentences.en: And they sponsor boutiques.
sentences.zh: 它们赞助精品店。

sentences.en: They sponsor hairdressers.
sentences.zh: 它们赞助美发沙龙。

sentences.en: They organize tours.
sentences.zh: 它们组织巡回活动。

sentences.en: And it's all, you know, you will attract the right boy.
sentences.zh: 这一切的核心就是，你知道的，你会吸引到合适的男孩。

sentences.en: You will be economically successful.
sentences.zh: 你会获得经济上的成功。

sentences.en: You will get a good job.
sentences.zh: 你会找到一份好工作。

sentences.en: You will do all this if you wear the right clothes and you have the right makeup.
sentences.zh: 只要你穿对衣服、化对妆，你就能做到这一切。

sentences.en: So those magazines are kind of working cahoots in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以这些杂志在某种程度上可以说是同流合污的。
